newsitem.title: UK: Britain opposes work standards link to freer trade.
newsitem.headline: Britain opposes work standards link to freer trade.

text.p: Britain said on Wednesday it would "vigorously" resist United States pressure for the issue of freeing world trade to be linked to acceptable labour standards in developing countries.

Trade and Industry Secretary Ian Lang said seeking such a link could merely slow down the dismantling of trade barriers around the world without improving the lot of exploited workers. Washington believes countries which use child, or forced, labour should be punished by trade sanctions.
It wants a ministerial meeting of the World Trade Organisation in Singapore in December to adopt a work programme which would include a link between working conditions and freer trade.

But Lang, in a speech to London's Royal Institute for International Affairs, said: "Britain will vigorously resist this linkage, which will only serve to slow down trade liberalisation and could even make social problems in the countries concerned even worse." "We are supported in this view by most of European industry and most other countries around the world," he added.

At a meeting in Luxembourg on Tuesday, EU trade ministers agreed to discuss the issue of labour standards in Singapore, but only to stress that the International Labour Organisation (ILO) was the best forum for the issue.
Lang said the WTO meeting should be the first step towards a complete liberalisation of world trade by the year 2020, which could dramatically improve prosperity in Britain and around the world.
He said Britain was "supportive" of the need to admit Russia, China and Taiwan to the WTO, but added: "They must accept WTO rules."
